title: An Explainable Genetic Algorithm-Optimized Weighted Soft Voting Framework for Heart Disease Prediction
content: Reliable and interpretable heart disease prediction across heterogeneous clinical cohorts remains a major barrier to clinical translation. This study presents an explainable, genetic-algorithm (GA)-optimized performance-weighted soft-voting (PWSV) framework for binary heart disease prediction using 920 records from the Cleveland, Hungary, Switzerland, and VA Long Beach cohorts. After data harmonization, leakage-aware preprocessing, and feature engineering, 29 encoded predictors were retained. GA independently optimized random forest, extra trees, radial basis function support vector machine, and gradient boosting using five-fold cross-validation confined to the development data. Each model’s mean cross-validated weighted F1-score was normalized into its ensemble weight, keeping both hyperparameter selection and weight estimation independent of the test data. Two complementary evaluation protocols were used: a stratified 80:20 development–test split to assess predictive performance and leave-one-dataset-out (LODO) validation to quantify cross-cohort generalizability. On the untouched test set, PWSV achieved 95.65% accuracy; disease-class precision, recall, and F1-score of 94.34%, 98.04%, and 96.15%, respectively; and a 98.11% area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, outperforming all optimized constituent classifiers. LODO accuracy ranged from 82.15% to 90.64%, revealing cohort-dependent performance variation that a random split alone would not capture. SHAP and LIME provided complementary global and patient-level explanations, and their aggregated feature rankings showed significant agreement (Spearman’s ρ = 0.867, p < 0.001). Overall, the framework integrates leakage-aware optimization, performance-driven probability fusion, source-aware validation, and concordant explanations within a reproducible pipeline. These findings support its potential for clinical decision support, while prospective multicenter validation remains necessary before deployment.
